semantic_changes: V6 is an authored semantic revision of router v5, not byte-equivalent to the original skill or a proven content-preserving compiler transformation.
Discovery frontmatter and both example references remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Only the two example references retain complete verbatim-source mappings.

Project creation and append must finish the complete generation-reference read as a separate tool action before project actions, then finish extension presence/configuration checks before setup. Setup remains separate from required context reads.

Append captures original bytes before a native edit and performs a separate full saved-artifact read after the last write. Comparison must verify the exact original prefix and checkbox states, the added item count, sequential IDs and unchecked new items; any later artifact change requires renewed verification.

Prewrite reads, edit diffs, successful writes and collector snapshots cannot stand in for model postwrite verification. Incomplete verification must be reported as incomplete with only the actual blocker.

Preservation claims require the completed postwrite read and byte comparison. Git history is unnecessary for this proof; attempted, failed or unavailable Git comparisons cannot be inferred from missing metadata or invented without invocation/result evidence.

All v5 hook selection and rendering templates, optional-hook authorization, condition skipping, setup arguments, native-write sandbox boundaries, feature-context/content guidance, neutral Gap questions, topic allocation and reviewer checkbox ownership remain unchanged.

validation_scope.offline: Package integrity; frozen predecessor, source, discovery and example retention; routed-reference availability; retained-source mapping and tamper rejection; exact preservation of hook selection/rendering, clarification and requirements-quality guidance. These checks do not test model instruction compliance. Checker/trace regressions are separate.
validation_scope.fidelity_claim: Unvalidated candidate. Instruction changes and deterministic offline tests do not prove model compliance, semantic equivalence, sandbox behavior on a future host or runtime savings.
